title: Personal Loans AutoPay Enrollment Rate: Calculation of the Rate in Force
content:
## Calculation

The rate in force from the enrollment date of a Personal Loans AutoPay enrollment is the loan's base interest rate less the grade's AutoPay discount, kept to two decimals, the rounding coming once, at the end.

This calculation applies to an enrollment on a loan with no hardship plan in active status that sets its own rate (a plan interest rate on the plan; a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit is such a plan), a loan holding at most one open hardship plan. On a loan whose active hardship plan sets its own rate the AutoPay discount never applies on top of that rate: while the plan is active the plan rate governs, so the rate in force from the enrollment date is the plan interest rate, and the discounted rate resumes when the plan ends if AutoPay is still on.

| AutoPay discount by grade | A | B | C | D | E | F | G |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| points | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.25 |

The base interest rate is the rate fixed at approval, shown on the loan record; it is not the current interest rate.

## Worked figures (hypothetical loans)

| Loan | Base interest rate | Active hardship plan with its own rate | Rate in force from enrollment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grade E | 20.00 | none | 20.00 less 0.25: 19.75 |
| Grade B | 11.30 | none | 11.30 less 0.50: 10.80 |
| Grade D | 17.00 | Temporary Rate Reduction Plan at 9.00 | 9.00 |
| Grade D | 17.00 | an active plan with no plan rate | 17.00 less 0.25: 16.75 |
